notes: Luhman 16 A and B (about 1.5 arcsec apart in this era) are one blended source at 6.15 arcsec per pixel.
Gaia DR3 has only a position for the pair (2-parameter solution). The proper motion and parallax used to place the cutouts are Bedin et al. 2024, not Gaia.
Frames matched to 1.27 um as for Epsilon Indi B (another L/T brown dwarf pair).

Detection: forced S/N in a 2 px aperture on the stack against the scatter of the same aperture at blank positions of that stack (reprojection correlates pixels, so a per-pixel noise would overstate S/N); needs S/N 5 and the centre within 1.5 px of the prediction.
No motion fit: 3 detected visits, expected drift 3.0 arcsec over the detected span (need 3 visits and half a pixel, 3.1 arcsec).
Each frame saw a different wavelength at the star's pixel (ranges per visit); a brightness change between visits mixes real change with colour. Not a light curve.
Per visit, only frames with no masked pixel in the aperture are averaged (frames_used); 0 visits had none, so their sums are lower limits.
Frame-to-frame scatter within a visit (scatter_mjy) is far above the VARIANCE error: the error bars understate the real uncertainty.
Photometry: forced 3 px (18.5 arcsec) radius aperture sum on each frame, local sky annulus, VARIANCE errors, no aperture correction, mean per visit.

differences.note: A visual aid: the later visit minus the earlier, at the same wavelength. Static stars leave residuals of up to about 17% of their peak (the PSF is undersampled), so a change under about 10% of a star's peak cannot be flagged. Distances must come from the motion fit, not from these patches.

target.name: Luhman 16
target.claim: Detected in every visit. No drift fit: the visits span about a year, and the expected 3.0 arcsec drift is under the half pixel (3.1 arcsec) the fit needs.
target.astrometry_source: Position: Gaia DR3 5353626573555863424 (G 16.92), a 2-parameter solution with no proper motion or parallax: Gaia lists only one blended source for the A+B pair. Proper motion and parallax: Bedin et al. 2024, Astron. Nachr. 345, e230158, as quoted on en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luhman_16 (CDS was down, so not checked in SIMBAD); Gaia DR3 archive TAP (gea.esac.esa.int, gaiadr3.gaia_source), fetched 2026-11-14
